content: For patients diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, the administration of basal insulin alone is typically inadequate because these individuals are entirely dependent on exogenous insulin for survival. Even during periods of fasting or when they are not consuming food, they frequently require a combination of basal insulin and prandial (mealtime) insulin to prevent the development of hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis. Additionally, these protocols should account for and adapt to the patient’s evolving insulin requirements during transitions in their care.
